days.title: Menstruation and Irregular Bleeding (Istihadah)
days.question: What is the difference between menstruation and istihadah? And what is forbidden for a woman during menstruation?
days.principle: Purification from menstruation is obligatory. Menstruation is a natural blood that the womb releases at known times without illness or injury; certain things are forbidden during menstruation, and none of them is forbidden during istihadah.

misconception.peopleSay: A woman with istihadah is exactly like a menstruating woman: she doesn't pray or fast.
misconception.correct: Nothing that is forbidden during menstruation is forbidden during istihadah; a woman with istihadah purifies herself and performs wudu for the time of each prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said to Fatimah bint Hubaysh: «إن ذلك عرق».

days.action: If someone in your home needs to know the difference between menstruation and istihadah, share the information exactly as it is in the book without adding to it, and if any details are unclear, direct them to ask the people of knowledge.
lesson: The book defines menstruation as natural blood that comes from the womb at known times without illness. Everything said in defining its minimum, maximum, beginning and end is a matter of ijtihad. Istihadah is blood that comes outside the time of menstruation; a woman with istihadah either has a habit she goes back to, or can distinguish the blood, or is confused and goes back to the usual habit of women. During menstruation, prayer, fasting, tawaf, touching the mushaf without a barrier, staying in the mosque and intercourse are forbidden. But none of these is forbidden during istihadah, and the Prophet ﷺ told Fatimah bint Hubaysh that it is a vein. Umm 'Atiyyah said they did not count brownish or yellowish discharge as anything after becoming pure.
days.quote: As for brownish and yellowish discharge, during the time of menstruation it is menstruation, and outside its time it counts for nothing.

quiz.question: A woman has istihadah bleeding (not menstruation). Does she stop praying?
options: No, istihadah forbids none of what menstruation forbids
quiz.explanation: She is the one from whom blood comes outside the time of menstruation.

quiz.question: A woman's period started while she was on Hajj. What does she do?
options: Do all the rites of Hajj except tawaf until she becomes pure

quiz.question: A woman saw yellowish or brownish discharge after becoming pure from her period. What is the ruling?
options: It counts for nothing because it is outside the time of menstruation
Istihadah from which she must perform ghusl
quiz.explanation: As for brownish and yellowish discharge, during the time of menstruation it is menstruation, and outside its time it counts for nothing.

days.title: Prayer Is the Pillar of Islam
days.question: Why does prayer have such a great status in the religion?
days.principle: Prayer is the central pole of the tent of Islam and its second pillar after the two testimonies; Allah made five prayers obligatory in the day and night. Whoever abandons it out of denial has disbelieved, and whether one who abandons it out of laziness is a disbeliever is a matter of ijtihad.

misconception.peopleSay: Prayer is a personal matter between a person and God, and not one of the essentials of the religion.
misconception.correct: Prayer is the central pole of the tent of Islam and its second pillar after the two testimonies; the command to establish it is so widespread in the Quran that it has become something known of the religion by necessity.

days.action: Try today to pray the five prayers on time, especially Fajr, whose recitation the verse says is witnessed.
lesson: Imagine a tent without the pole in its middle: it would surely fall. The book says prayer is that pole for Islam. Whoever prays it as Allah commanded will have light, salvation and proof on the Day of Resurrection. The book distinguishes between one who abandons it out of denial, which is disbelief, and one who abandons it out of laziness, whose being a disbeliever is a matter of ijtihad. The Quran is full of verses commanding us to establish prayer and guard it, especially the middle prayer. Allah made establishing prayer a sign of brotherhood in religion. And the Companions did not see abandoning any deed as disbelief except abandoning prayer, as 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq said.
days.quote: The command to establish prayer is so widespread in the Noble Quran that it has become something known of the religion by necessity, needing no proofs to be cited for it.

quiz.question: Someone denies that prayer is obligatory. What is his ruling?
options: A disbeliever, because its obligation is known of the religion by necessity
quiz.explanation: The command to establish prayer is so widespread in the Noble Quran that it has become something known of the religion by necessity, needing no proofs to be cited for it.

quiz.question: Someone believes prayer is obligatory but abandons it out of laziness. What is the ruling?
options: A Muslim who will not be held accountable
Whether he is a disbeliever is a matter of ijtihad among scholars
quiz.explanation: And whoever abandons it out of laziness, whether he is a disbeliever is a matter of ijtihad.

quiz.question: What does guarding the prayer give a person on the Day of Resurrection?

askTheBook: Why is prayer the pillar of Islam?
What is the ruling on abandoning prayer?
What is the virtue of guarding the prayer?

days.title: The Conditions of Prayer
days.question: What must be in place for prayer to be obligatory on me and for my prayer to be valid?
days.principle: The conditions for prayer to be obligatory are Islam, puberty, sanity and the entry of its time; the conditions for it to be valid are intention, purity from ritual impurity and filth, covering the 'awrah and facing the qiblah.
days.action: Before each prayer today, quickly check the conditions in your head: Do I have wudu? Are my clothes and place clean? Am I properly covered? Am I facing the qiblah? Do I intend this prayer?
lesson: Before prayer is required of you, you must be Muslim, past puberty and sane, and its time must have entered; these are the conditions of obligation. The Prophet ﷺ commanded Mu'adh to call to the two testimonies first, before prayer, so that Islam would be established and the obligation would then be valid. Then, for your prayer to be accepted, you must have the intention, be pure from ritual impurity and filth, have your 'awrah covered and face the qiblah. Intention before prayer is a condition and within it a pillar, and the Prophet ﷺ said that actions are only by intentions. The verse ﴿خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ﴾ is evidence that covering the 'awrah is obligatory, because in the Jahiliyyah people used to perform tawaf naked.
days.quote: So he commanded him to call to the two testimonies first, so that the bond of Islam would be established for them, and it would then be valid to require prayer and the rest of the laws of Islam of them.

quiz.question: Someone prayed Dhuhr half an hour before the adhan. Is his prayer valid?
options: Yes, what matters is that he prayed
No, the entry of the time is a condition for prayer being obligatory
Yes, if he was in a hurry
quiz.explanation: The conditions for it being obligatory are: Islam, puberty, sanity and the entry of its time.

quiz.question: Someone prayed in clothes that did not cover his 'awrah. Is his prayer valid?
options: No, covering the 'awrah is a condition for the prayer to be valid
Yes, clothing has nothing to do with it
quiz.explanation: In it is evidence that covering the 'awrah in prayer is obligatory.

quiz.question: What is the ruling of intention in prayer?
options: It must be said out loud
Before prayer it is a condition, and within prayer it is a pillar
quiz.explanation: (Before prayer it is a condition, and within prayer it is a pillar.)

askTheBook: What are the conditions for prayer being obligatory?
What are the conditions for prayer being valid?
What is the evidence that covering the 'awrah in prayer is obligatory?

days.title: The Pillars of Prayer: Pray as You Have Seen Me Pray
days.question: What are the essential parts of prayer that, if left out, make the prayer invalid?
days.principle: The pillars of prayer are: standing in obligatory prayers for whoever is able, the opening takbir, reciting al-Fatihah, bowing and rising from it, prostrating and rising from it, sitting between the two prostrations, tranquillity, the final tashahhud and sitting for it, the taslim, and doing these pillars in order.

misconception.peopleSay: What matters is finishing the prayer; it doesn't matter whether I'm still in bowing and prostration.
misconception.correct: Tranquillity (tuma'ninah) is one of the pillars of prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said to the man who did not pray with tranquillity: «ارجع فصل فإنك لم تصل», and he likened one who pecks in his prostration to a hungry man who eats only a date or two.

days.action: In every prayer today, remain still in bowing and prostration until every limb settles in its place, as the Prophet ﷺ taught the man who prayed badly.
lesson: The pillars of prayer are the columns without any one of which the prayer cannot stand, and the book lists them one by one. Whoever cannot stand prays sitting, and if he cannot, then lying on his side. In the hadith of the man who prayed badly, the Prophet ﷺ sent the man back to pray three times until he taught him to be still in every pillar. The Prophet ﷺ saw a man pecking in his prostration and likened him to a hungry man eating a date or two that do him no good. Hudhayfah told a man who did not complete his bowing and prostration that he had not prayed. Sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ in the final tashahhud is disputed: some said it is a pillar and some said it is a sunnah.
days.quote: This hadith mentions some of the pillars, such as the opening takbir and the taslim, and some of the sunnahs, as in the rest of the hadith.

quiz.question: Someone prays very quickly without remaining still in bowing and prostration. Is his prayer valid?
options: Yes, what matters is that he prayed
Valid if he is in a hurry

quiz.question: A sick person cannot stand in the obligatory prayer. What does he do?
options: The prayer is dropped for him
He prays sitting, and if he cannot, he prays on his side
He must stand even if it harms him
He delays it until he recovers

quiz.question: What is the ruling on sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ in the final tashahhud?
options: Disputed: some said it is a pillar and some said it is a sunnah
quiz.explanation: There is disagreement about sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ in the final tashahhud: some said it is one of the pillars and some said it is one of the sunnahs.

days.title: What Invalidates Prayer, and Its Sunnahs
days.question: What ruins the prayer? And what are the sunnahs that complete it?
days.principle: Prayer is invalidated by deliberately leaving out a pillar, by eating and drinking, by speaking for a purpose other than correcting it, by laughing aloud, and by excessive movement without necessity. Among its sunnahs are the opening supplication, saying "amin" and reciting what is easy of the Quran after al-Fatihah.

misconception.peopleSay: Any smile in prayer invalidates it.
misconception.correct: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah said: A smile does not break the prayer; only laughing aloud breaks it.

days.action: Memorise the opening supplication («اللهم باعد بيني وبين خطاياي...») and say it at the start of your prayer today.
lesson: Prayer can become invalid if a person deliberately leaves out a pillar, eats or drinks, speaks words not meant to correct the prayer, laughs aloud, or makes a lot of movement without necessity. The Prophet ﷺ said that the ordinary speech of people is not fit for the prayer; it is glorification, takbir and recitation of the Quran. Jabir said that a smile does not break the prayer; what breaks it is laughing aloud. Among the sunnahs of prayer is seeking refuge from Shaytan, and the opening supplication the Prophet ﷺ used to say between the takbir and the recitation. Also saying "amin" after al-Fatihah, which means "O Allah, answer"; whoever's amin coincides with the amin of the angels, his previous sins are forgiven. Among the sunnahs is reciting what is easy after al-Fatihah, reciting aloud in the loud prayers and quietly in the quiet ones.
days.quote: So seeking refuge is a sunnah according to the generality of the Salaf, because of these texts.

quiz.question: Someone laughed out loud during the prayer. What about his prayer?
options: He only performs the prostration of forgetfulness
quiz.explanation: A smile does not break the prayer; only laughing aloud breaks it.

quiz.question: Someone deliberately spoke ordinary words with someone while praying. What is the ruling on his prayer?
options: It is invalidated, because the prayer has no place for people's ordinary speech

quiz.question: When the imam says "wa lad-dallin" and you say "amin", what does it mean?
quiz.explanation: The meaning of amin: O Allah, answer.

askTheBook: What invalidates the prayer?

days.title: The Remaining Sunnahs, and What Is Disputed
days.question: What sunnahs did the Prophet ﷺ do in his prayer? And what did the scholars differ about?
days.principle: Among the sunnahs of prayer are raising the hands in their places, placing the right hand over the left while standing, and praying towards a sutrah. There is disagreement over saying "sami'a Allahu liman hamidah" and "rabbana wa lakal-hamd", saying the glorification in bowing and prostration once, the takbirs of transition and the first tashahhud: some said they are obligatory and some said they are sunnahs.

misconception.peopleSay: The tashahhud has only one wording, and any other wording is wrong.
misconception.correct: The tashahhud has been reported in several wordings from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Musa, and the scholars agree that all these wordings are permissible; whichever one the person praying says suffices.

days.action: Memorise the wording of the tashahhud in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, and go over it to yourself in your prayer today.
lesson: Among the sunnahs of prayer is raising the hands at the opening takbir, at bowing and when rising from it, as Ibn 'Umar described the Prophet's ﷺ prayer. Also placing the right hand over the left while standing. Among the sunnahs is praying towards a sutrah, the minimum of which is like the back of a camel saddle; al-Nawawi said it is about two-thirds of a forearm's length, and it is achieved with anything placed in front of you. There are things the scholars differed on, whether obligatory or sunnah, such as "sami'a Allahu liman hamidah", saying the glorification in bowing and prostration once, and the first tashahhud. The tashahhud has been reported in more than one wording, and the scholars agree that any of them suffices. The book presents both sides' evidence on the first tashahhud and says both are plausible.
days.quote: Al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This hadith shows that it is recommended to have a sutrah in front of the person praying.

quiz.question: Someone said a wording of the tashahhud different from the one you are used to, but it is reported. What about his prayer?
quiz.explanation: The scholars agree that all these wordings are permissible; whichever one the person praying says suffices.

quiz.question: You are praying in a place where people walk past. What is the sunnah?
options: There is no sunnah about this
Pray in the middle of the path
Pray towards a sutrah in front of you
quiz.explanation: Al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This hadith shows that it is recommended to have a sutrah in front of the person praying.

quiz.question: What is the ruling on raising the hands with the opening takbir and at bowing?
options: A pillar without which the prayer is invalid

days.title: What Is Disliked in Prayer, and the Prostration of Forgetfulness
days.question: What things are disliked in prayer? And if I forget or make a mistake, what do I do?
days.principle: Among the disliked things in prayer are turning around, raising the gaze to the sky, fidgeting, holding back the call of nature and praying when food is served. The prostration of forgetfulness is prescribed for an addition to or omission from the prayer, or doubt about that.

misconception.peopleSay: The prostration of forgetfulness must be after the taslim only, never before it.
misconception.correct: The prostration of forgetfulness may be done before or after the taslim, and the matter is broad. It is better, if it is for an omission, to do it before the taslim, and if it is for an addition, after the taslim.

days.action: Before you begin your prayer today, make sure you are not hungry with food in front of you or needing the toilet, so that you pray with a present heart.
lesson: The book lists the disliked things in prayer: turning around, raising the gaze to the sky, putting the hands on the hips, interlacing and cracking the fingers, fidgeting, and praying when food is served or when one needs the toilet. The Prophet ﷺ described turning around as a theft that Shaytan steals from a servant's prayer. Then it speaks about the prostration of forgetfulness, which is prescribed if there is an addition, omission or doubt. Whoever doubts the number of units builds on the lower number and prostrates for forgetfulness. It may be done before or after the taslim, and the matter is broad; it is better before the taslim for an omission and after it for an addition. The Prophet ﷺ himself made mistakes: he prayed Dhuhr as five units, and gave the taslim after two units in 'Asr, and prostrated for forgetfulness.
days.quote: Because it repairs the prayer so that it is completed; and if it is for an addition, after the taslim, because it humiliates Shaytan, so as not to combine two additions in the prayer.

quiz.question: Someone praying is unsure whether he prayed 3 or 4 units. What does he do?
options: Build on the lower number (3) and prostrate for forgetfulness
quiz.explanation: Whoever doubts the number of units builds on the lower number and prostrates for forgetfulness.

quiz.question: He forgot the first tashahhud (an omission). When does he prostrate for forgetfulness?
options: Preferably before the taslim, and the matter is broad
It must be after the taslim
quiz.explanation: It is better, if it is for an omission, to be before the taslim, because it repairs the prayer so that it is completed.

quiz.question: Someone turns around a lot in his prayer. What is the ruling?
options: Disliked, because it is a theft by Shaytan

days.title: Congregational Prayer and Friday Prayer
days.question: Why does Islam strongly emphasise congregational prayer and Friday prayer?
days.principle: Congregational prayer is required and is twenty-seven degrees better than praying alone. The one who leads the people is the one most versed in the Book of Allah. The Friday prayer is obligatory on every adult, healthy, resident Muslim, and it is a sermon and two units after midday.

misconception.peopleSay: A good imam is one who makes the prayer very long, even if the people behind him get tired.
misconception.correct: Whoever leads people should keep it light, for among them are the weak, the sick and those with needs. The Prophet ﷺ was angry with someone who made it long for the people and said: «إن منكم منفرين، فأيكم أم الناس فليوجز».

days.action: Try today to pray at least one obligatory prayer in congregation, and remember that it is twenty-seven degrees better than praying alone.
lesson: The book stresses that congregational prayer is required, and that it is better than praying alone by twenty-seven degrees. The Prophet ﷺ threatened those who stayed away from it severely, and Ibn Mas'ud said no one stayed away from it except a known hypocrite. The one who leads the people is the one most versed in the Book of Allah, then the most knowledgeable of the Sunnah. The imam must keep it light, because behind him are the elderly, the weak and those with needs, and the Prophet ﷺ was very angry with an imam who made it long for people. As for Friday, Allah commanded us, when the call to prayer is made, to hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. The Prophet ﷺ warned those who abandon the Friday prayers that Allah would seal their hearts.

quiz.question: You are the imam and among those behind you are elderly and sick people. Do you make it long or light?
options: Light, because among them are the weak and those with needs
Long, because the reward is greater

quiz.question: Who is most entitled to lead people in prayer?
options: The one most versed in the Book of Allah
The one with the loudest voice

quiz.question: How does congregational prayer differ from praying alone?
options: It is better by twenty-seven degrees

days.title: The Regular Sunnah Prayers, and the Concession to Combine and Shorten
days.question: Which sunnah prayers did the Prophet ﷺ keep up alongside the obligatory ones? And how do I pray when travelling?
days.principle: The regular sunnah prayers the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept up were two units before Fajr, two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib and two after 'Isha', in addition to the witr. Shortening the four-unit prayers while travelling is an established sunnah, and combining is an occasional concession.

misconception.peopleSay: Shortening prayer while travelling was only in times of fear and war, and is pointless now.
misconception.correct: Ya'la ibn Umayyah asked 'Umar about shortening when people were safe, and 'Umar asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: «صدقة تصدق الله بها عليكم فاقبلوا صدقته».

days.action: If you are not used to the regular sunnah prayers, start today with the two units before Fajr, because Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ was not more diligent about any voluntary prayer than about them.
lesson: The Prophet ﷺ kept up sunnah prayers alongside the obligatory ones: two units before Fajr, two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib, two after 'Isha', and the witr. Aisha said there was no voluntary prayer he was keener on than the two units of Fajr. The night prayer is in pairs, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded us to make the last of our night prayer witr. When travelling, shortening the four-unit prayers is an established sunnah, while combining is an occasional concession, and there is a well-known disagreement about the distance for shortening. The Prophet ﷺ called shortening a charity from Allah to us and commanded us to accept it. When he ﷺ was in a hurry while travelling, he would combine Dhuhr with 'Asr and Maghrib with 'Isha', and Mu'adh said he did so in order not to cause hardship to his Ummah.

quiz.question: A traveller shortens Dhuhr to two units. Is that a concession or a sunnah?
options: Shortening the four-unit prayers while travelling is an established sunnah, a charity Allah has given us

quiz.question: What is the ruling on combining two prayers?
options: A permanent sunnah on every journey
An occasional concession used when needed
quiz.explanation: And that combining is an occasional concession.

quiz.question: Which regular sunnah prayer did the Prophet ﷺ keep up most?

days.title: The Two 'Eid Prayers
days.question: How do we pray the 'Eid prayer? And does the joy of 'Eid have a place in the religion?
days.principle: The two 'Eid prayers are among the rites of Islam; scholars differed on whether they are a communal obligation, obligatory, or an emphasised sunnah. They are two units without adhan or iqamah, followed by the 'Eid sermon, which comes after the prayer by consensus.

misconception.peopleSay: 'Eid is only serious worship, with no place in it for joy and play.
misconception.correct: Play that involves no sin is permitted, because showing joy on the two 'Eids is one of the rites of the religion. The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن لكل قوم عيداً وهذا عيدنا».

days.action: On the next 'Eid, go out to the 'Eid prayer with your family, and openly show the takbir and the joy of 'Eid in your home with something permissible.
lesson: The two 'Eid prayers are among the rites of Islam, and scholars differed on whether they are a communal obligation, obligatory, or an emphasised sunnah. They are two units without adhan or iqamah, with seven takbirs in the first and five in the second, followed by the sermon. The sunnah is to pray it in an open space; the Prophet ﷺ used to go out to the prayer ground and did not pray it in the mosque without an excuse. It is sunnah to say the takbir openly on the nights of 'Eid, and it is recommended that all women go out to the prayer ground to witness the good and the Muslims' supplication, with menstruating women keeping away from the prayer area itself. Joy on 'Eid is one of the rites of the religion; the Prophet ﷺ allowed permissible singing on 'Eid and said every people has an 'Eid and this is ours. He also let Aisha watch the Abyssinians playing with spears on the day of 'Eid.
days.quote: Play that involves no sin is permitted, because showing joy on the two 'Eids is one of the rites of the religion.

quiz.question: On 'Eid, your friend says: "Play and celebration don't suit religious people." What is the correct understanding?
options: Showing joy on 'Eid is one of the rites of the religion, and permissible play is allowed
quiz.explanation: Play that involves no sin is permitted, because showing joy on the two 'Eids is one of the rites of the religion.

quiz.question: Is the 'Eid sermon before or after the prayer?
quiz.explanation: Then the 'Eid sermon follows, and it is after the prayer by consensus.

quiz.question: Does the 'Eid prayer have an adhan and iqamah?
options: No, it is two units without adhan or iqamah
quiz.explanation: It is two units without adhan or iqamah.
